rival_node: C6 (Items in GW are items in Working Memory)
note: FMT: workspace = channel occupancy = working memory. Diverges on whether broadcast constitutes experience (B4).

rival_node: B1 (GW operates as information bottleneck: entry is gated)
note: FMT derives the bottleneck as a low-rank channel and its width as WM capacity (F3).

rival_node: B4 (Attentional processes mobilize information and broadcast it into the GW)
note: Attention = selection into the channel; experience = closure over it.

rival_node: D6 (failed ignition should not be conscious)
note: FMT allows minimal and basic consciousness without global broadcast (§3.4.6).

rival_node: C5 (Attention and availability for report are not necessary for consciousness)
note: Agreement on no-report; disagreement on sufficiency of local recurrence (FMT B4).

rival_node: D11 (Artificial and biological systems with a functionally equivalent GW are conscious)
note: FMT: a workspace without closure and free modelling is not enough (D9).

rival_node: D2 (Artificial and biological systems with recurrent architecture that enables learning and perceptual organization are conscious)
note: FMT: recurrence hosts the second level (A2) but closure (A3) and free modelling (A1) are also required.

rival_node: F3 (extrapolation to other populations, e.g. artificial systems)
note: FMT is substrate-independent; a digital implementation meeting the sufficient conjunction (B5) is conscious.
FMT: experience is in the running explicit models; idle units contribute only via the implicit substrate.

rival_node: C2 (type of experience depends on the architecture of the substrate specifying the cause-effect structure)
note: Both make experienced quality structure-dependent; FMT locates the structure at the running level and predicts that absolute encoding does not transfer (F2).

rival_node: A1 / B5 (higher-order state indexes first-order states as reliably reflecting the world)
relation: agrees on the function, contradicts on constitution
note: FMT needs source distinguishability but posits no tag, and denies that the tag constitutes experience (imagery is experienced).

rival_node: F3 (visual hallucinations if prefrontal functions are disrupted)
note: Both predict reality-monitoring failure under perturbation; FMT adds the ordering (attribution degrades before experience).

rival_node: PRM D2 (change in the higher-order state changes consciousness with the first-order state constant)
note: FMT: metacognitive read-out is separable from experience (F4); only disruption of closure should change experience.
